title: Hearing to take place in inquest into death
article: The province announced Thursday a standing hearing will take place to determine who can participate in the upcoming inquest into the death of 27-year-old Winnipegger Aaron Ross.
Ross, the province said in a statement, died on Sept. 30, 2019 at St. Boniface Hospital, days after an interaction with Winnipeg police where he was detained and subsequently taken to the Hospital.

An obituary for Ross reads in part, "Aaron was born on February 29, 1992 in Winnipeg, Manitoba after a difficult birth which caused complications that he fought with dignity his whole life. Aaron was a member of the Bloodvein First Nation and was proud of his heritage."
The CBC reported on the Ross's death, saying in part he was "naked and behaving erratically near the riverbank in Winnipeg moments before police restrained him and he became unresponsive."
Arresting officers were cleared of wrongdoing.

Under the Fatality Inquiries Act, an inquest has been called by Manitoba's Chief Medical Examiner. Inquests investigate the circumstances and events leading to fatalities to ascertain what, if anything, might be done to prevent similar deaths in the future.
